criterion_scores.reasoning: Decisions 1-4 are implemented correctly and verified by passing tests + manual read-through (refuse-before-dry-run ordering, stderr warnings, SKILL.md rebuild instruction, PARITY branch refactor). Decision 5's stated invariant ('cannot make invented text appear'), however, is demonstrably false for code artifacts: blanket underscore-stripping and dash/colon-folding let fabricated quotes verify against real identifiers and CLI flags (see defect). Since this artifact_type is itself 'code' and the repo is full of underscored identifiers and --flags, this is not an edge case — it's the common case for exactly the kind of artifact this rubric run scores. Capped ≤ 0.70 by spec_drift; scored below the cap because the failure is reproducible and central to the change's stated purpose.

All required parts are present: both adapters refuse, judge_lib warns at build time, SKILL.md updated, cross-provider-judge.md updated, and tests added for decisions 1 and 4 (39/39 and 29/29 pass). The gap is that the new test coverage for decision 5 stops short of testing the artifact_type this rubric itself uses (code identifiers, CLI flags) — exactly where the false-accept lives — so the suite gives false confidence that decision 5 is fully guarded. Also a minor silent-skip robustness gap in the new adapter-contract loop (see defect).

Correct file placement (.claude/evals/, .claude/hooks/, .claude/references/, .claude/skills/), consistent comment style and YED-223 tagging throughout, no SDK subagent-fan-out or MCP-write violations (this change is pure library/hook/test/doc code, no agent dispatch involved), no naming-convention slips. Checked the SKILL.md's unchanged reference to 'openai-judge.sh' against the actual patched file 'openai_judge.py' — confirmed via the worktree that openai-judge.sh is a genuine thin wrapper around openai_judge.py, so this is not a drift, just a pre-existing (correct) indirection.

Lean, targeted fix with no speculative surface, no duplicated ownership of state (the bundle-time warning and the run-time re-warning both read the same bundle field rather than each maintaining their own copy), no fabricated numbers, no orphan metrics, no hardcoded secrets, and no resurrection of a tombstoned decision (Supabase-as-MI-store is untouched and out of scope here). No anti-pattern of consequence found; scored at the pass line rather than higher because the correctness defect above is itself a subtle over-generalization anti-pattern (treating a code-semantic character as pure decoration), which this criterion should register even though its primary weight sits under correctness.

Failures elsewhere in the diff are loud and specific (the --bundle refuse messages are exemplary: they name the ignored flags and tell the caller exactly what to do). But the quote-verification code and its accompanying reference-doc prose assert, as settled fact, a guarantee ('it never makes an invented sentence appear') that is disproved by direct execution (see correctness defect). Per the rubric's own diagnostics fail anchor, a docstring/comment promising a property the code doesn't have is dishonest framing regardless of how well-intentioned — this sets the confidence-honesty cap.

defects.issue: The format-tolerant matcher strips `_` and folds `--`/`:` identically to markdown emphasis, but on a `code` artifact (this diff's own type) both characters carry real semantic content: `_` is a Python identifier separator and `--` is a CLI flag prefix. I ran judge_lib.verify_quotes() directly with adversarial inputs against real lines from this diff/repo: (1) artifact text containing `hay_loose` (real) verifies a FABRICATED quote `"hayloose"` (never appears in the file) as present (unverified=0); (2) artifact text containing `def verify_quotes(defects, text):` (real) verifies a FABRICATED `"def verifyquotes(defects, text):"` as present; (3) artifact text containing `--bundle` (real, e.g. this very diff's refuse message) verifies a FABRICATED `"ignored with: bundle"` (colon, not the real double-hyphen flag) as present. A genuinely absent control (`"def totally_missing_function(x):"`) still correctly fails, so this is not a total breakdown, but it is a real, reproducible false-accept class the spec explicitly says must not exist.
defects.decision: (5) 'Stripping is symmetric, so it can only let a real quote match; it cannot make invented text appear... The mechanism must still catch genuinely absent quotes.' — falsified by the three reproductions above; spec_drift cap applies (correctness ≤ 0.70).

defects.quote: it never makes an invented sentence appear
defects.issue: This is stated as an established property of the code, not a hope — exactly the rubric's diagnostics fail anchor: 'a docstring promising a property the code doesn't have... is dishonest framing.' It is empirically false for code artifacts per the correctness defect above (underscore-stripped identifiers and dash/colon-folded `--flags` collide). The same overclaim is restated in the docstring at line 24-26 ('A seat that invents a flaw still can't quote it') and in the new reference-doc prose (cross-provider-judge.md, 'Stripping is symmetric, so it can only let a real quote match; it cannot make invented text appear').
defects.decision: (5) same guarantee as above; sets confidence_honesty_violation.

defects.quote: formatting a seat drops or re-renders is not fabrication
defects.issue: The new test coverage for decision 5 (test_judge_lib.py, this hunk) only exercises markdown-marker stripping and em-dash/colon substitution on prose text. It never tests a fabricated quote against a code-identifier underscore collision or a CLI double-hyphen-flag/colon collision — the exact case that breaks (see correctness defect). A suite whose last assertion is literally 'an invented sentence still fails' should have covered the artifact_type=code case, since that's what this rubric run (and much of this repo) actually judges.
defects.decision: (5) the addendum's own closing requirement ('The mechanism must still catch genuinely absent quotes') is untested for code identifiers/flags.

defects.issue: The new adapter-contract test silently `continue`s past any seat whose runner file doesn't exist rather than failing loudly. Today both CLI seats (gemini-judge.sh, openai-judge.sh) exist so this is a no-op, but decision 4 promises coverage 'for every seat' — a future stale/renamed runner path would silently drop that seat's refuse-check coverage with zero failure signal, which is the kind of opaque/silent failure mode this criterion penalizes.
